<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflict and attacks
*[[Abha International Airport attack]]
**A ballistic missile fired by [[Houthi]] forces strikes the arrivals hall at [[Abha International Airport]] in [[Saudi Arabia]], injuring 26 people. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/06/12/middleeast/saudi-airport-houthi-missile-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**Militants kill five [[Paramilitary forces of India|Indian paramilitary police]] in [[Anantnag district]]. Three paramilitaries, a local policeman and a woman bystander are wounded, and one militant is killed. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/terrorists-attack-police-party-in-jammu-and-kashmirs-anantnag-2052165 (NDTV)]
*[[2018–19 Sudanese protests|Sudanese protests]]
**[[Sudanese military]] and opposition leaders agree to resume talks that broke down after a [[Khartoum massacre|violent crackdown on protesters]] earlier in June. The military also agrees to release political prisoners, while the opposition agrees to end its campaign of strikes and civil disobedience. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-48602868 (BBC News)]
*[[Terrorism in Australia]]
**Clavell brothers rammed a [[Police car|police car]] and then lunged at police [[Stabbing as a terrorist tactic|with a knife]] and a [[Tomahawk|tomahawk]] before they were shot on Wednesday afternoon by [[Victoria Police|Victorian police]]. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/barnawartha-albury-police-shooting-two-men-suspected-terror-links-nsw-victoria-police-news-australia/f2b85b9a-d91b-4a67-91b5-062d4ad83d7d (9News)]
;Business and finance
*[[China–United States trade war]]
**Chinese telecommunications and electronics company [[Huawei]] cancels its new laptop launch. A Huawei executive said the company has been "unable to supply the PC" because of the  U.S. trade blacklist and may have to scrap the project. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-48609747 (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2019/may/19/google-huawei-trump-blacklist-report (''The Guardian'')]
;Disasters and accidents
*[[Bolivarian diaspora]]
**A speedboat carrying migrants reportedly sinks off the coast of [[Venezuela]] ''en route'' to [[Curaçao]], making it the third migrant boat leaving Venezuela to sink in as many months, with over 50 people missing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-48607330 (BBC News)]
*[[2019 Indian Air Force An-32 crash|Indian Air Force An-32 crash]]
** The wreckage of An-32 aircraft was found in [[Arunachal Pradesh]] with all 13 people on board killed. [https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/an32-crash-site-arunachal-iaf-black-box-recorder-1548103-2019-06-13 (''India Today'')]
;Health and environment
*[[2018–19 Kivu Ebola epidemic|Kivu Ebola epidemic]]
** [[Wellcome Trust]] director [[Jeremy Farrar|Dr. Jeremy Farrar]] says the Ebola outbreak in eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], which has killed 1,400 people since August 2018, is the worst since the [[Western African Ebola virus epidemic|2013–2016 outbreak in West Africa]] and shows "no sign of stopping". Uganda reported its first two deaths. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-48615667 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Japan–United States relations]], [[Iran–Japan relations]], [[Iran–United States relations]]
**[[Japan]] offers to mediate between Iran and the U.S.; officials say the Japanese government hopes to rescue the landmark 2015 international nuclear deal. [https://financialtribune.com/articles/national/97908/japan-offers-to-mediate-between-iran-us (''Financial Tribune'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-japan-usa/iran-to-ask-japans-abe-to-mediate-over-us-oil-sanctions-officials-idUSKCN1TD0RJ (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Reuters]] reports, on the basis of an unnamed "senior administration" source, that the administration of [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] is pressuring the government of [[Saudi Arabia]] to show some progress in its investigation of the [[Assassination of Jamal Khashoggi|murder]] of [[Jamal Khashoggi]] before the one-year anniversary in October. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-khashoggi-usa/u-s-pushes-for-saudi-progress-on-khashoggi-probe-before-anniversary-of-killing-idUSKCN1TC2RY (Reuters)]
*[[Trial of Catalonia independence leaders]]
**The trial of the leaders involved in the [[Catalan declaration of independence]] ends and is remitted to decision. A verdict is not expected until after August. [https://www.euronews.com/2019/06/12/last-day-of-trial-for-catalan-leaders (Euronews)]
*Two [[Canada|Canadian]] women who were abducted in [[Ghana]] are rescued by Ghanaian police. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/ottawa-very-relieved-after-2-canadian-women-abducted-in-ghana-rescued-1.4462634 (CTV News)]
*Aftermath of the [[2019 college admissions bribery scandal]]
**Former [[Stanford University]] sailing coach John Vandemoer is sentenced to two-years [[United States federal probation and supervised release|probation]], with the first six months to be served under [[house arrest]]. Vandemoer is the first person to be sentenced among the 50 individuals indicted on federal charges related to the U.S. college admissions bribery scheme. [https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-college-admissions-scandal-stanford-john-vandemoer-sentenced-20190612-story.html (''Los Angeles Times'')] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2019/06/12/no-prison-first-defendant-bribery-scandal-college/1429812001/ (''USA Today'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/06/12/us/college-admissions-scandal-stanford.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Same-sex marriage in Ecuador]]
**The [[Supreme Court of Ecuador]] legalizes same-sex marriage. [https://www.france24.com/en/20190613-ecuador-highest-court-approves-same-sex-marriage (France24)]
*[[Abortion in the United States by state]]
**[[Governor of Illinois|Illinois Governor]] [[J. B. Pritzker]] signs abortion rights law making the procedure a "fundamental right" for pregnant individuals in the state. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/politics/ct-met-illinois-abortion-rights-law-governor-jb-pritzker-20190612-story.html (''Chicago Tribune'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Hong Kong anti-extradition bill protests|Hong Kong extradition law controversy]]
**The [[Legislative Council of Hong Kong|Legislative Council]] delays "to a later time" the second reading of the new legislation on  extradition as  thousands of protesters, who blocked key roads around government buildings, were confronted by police  in [[Riot control|riot gear]] using [[pepper spray]]. Despite widespread opposition, the government had said it will continue to push for passage. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-48591001 (BBC News)]
*[[Media freedom in Russia]]
**[[Russia]]n authorities  detain hundreds of protesters, including ''[[Novaya Gazeta]]'' journalist and protest organizer Ilya Azar and other reporters, at an "unauthorized march" in [[Moscow]] demanding punishment for police who detained anti-corruption journalist [[Ivan Golunov]].  Golunov's charges were dropped and he was released yesterday at which time [[Ministry of Internal Affairs (Russia)|Interior Minister]] [[Vladimir Kolokoltsev]] said some officers who had taken part in his detention were  suspended pending an investigation. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48607317 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-journalist-free/russia-in-rare-u-turn-after-public-anger-drops-case-against-journalist-idUSKCN1TC1QW (Reuters)]
*The House Oversight Committee votes to hold [[United States Attorney General|Attorney General]] [[William Barr]] and [[United States Secretary of Commerce|Commerce Secretary]] [[Wilbur Ross]] in contempt after [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] asserted executive privilege over materials related to the committee's census investigation. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/ag-barr-trump-invoke-privilege-census-materials-dems/story?id=63639998 (ABC News)]
*[[Operation Car Wash]]
**More text messages between judge [[Sérgio Moro]] and prosecutor [[Deltan Dallagnol]] are leaked, implicating Vice-President of the [[Supreme Federal Court]] [[Luiz Fux]] in illicit collaboration between [[Brazil|Brazilian]] judges and Car Wash's team of prosecutors. [https://veja.abril.com.br/politica/in-fux-we-trust-disse-moro-a-deltan-em-mensagem-vazada/ (Veja)]
*[[Bolivarian diaspora]]
**The Peruvian Catholic Church urges the government of that country to continue receiving Venezuelan immigrants. He also expressed concern about the "increase in the negative perception of migrants." This, after the president [[Martín Vizcarra]] decided to demand visa and passport for Venezuelan citizens who wish to enter Peru. [https://gestion.pe/mundo/iglesia-pide-peru-siga-acogiendo-venezolanos-visa-269969 (Gestión)]

;Science and technology
*[[List of nearest exoplanets]], [[Doppler Spectroscopy]]
**A study on exoplanet populations combining decades of data from several different observatories detects 118 possible exoplanets orbiting nearby [[red dwarf]]s, including new [[Discoveries of exoplanets|discoveries]] around nearby stars [[Wolf 359]], [[Lacaille 9352]], [[Struve 2398]] B, and [[Luyten's Star]]. [https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.04644 (Arxiv)] <!--keep this source until a news source can be found, it's bound to get on the news anyway and there's no explicit rules against using non-news sources-->
*Despite dense [[fog]], [[SpaceX]] successfully launches the [[Canadian Space Agency]]'s [[RADARSAT Constellation]] satellites on a [[Falcon 9]] rocket from [[Vandenberg Air Force Base]]. [https://www.cnet.com/news/spacex-pulls-off-dazzling-falcon-9-launch-in-thick-fog/ (CNET)]

;Sports
*[[2019 Stanley Cup Finals]]
**In [[National Hockey League|ice hockey]], the [[St. Louis Blues]] defeat the [[Boston Bruins]] four games to three to win their first [[Stanley Cup]]. [https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/news/stanley-cup-final-2019-blues-stifle-bruins-4-1-in-game-7-to-win-first-title-in-team-history/ (CBS Sports)]
